source.text: Ὅτε οὖν ἐπαυσάμην ἐρωτῶν αὐτὴν περὶ πάντων τούτων, λέγει μοι· Θέλεις ἄλλο ἰδεῖν; κατεπίθυμος ὢν τοῦ θεάσασθαι περιχαρὴς ἐγενόμην τοῦ ἰδεῖν. 2. ἐμβλέψασά μοι ὑπεμειδίασεν καὶ λέγει μοι· Βλέπεις ἑπτὰ γυναῖκας κύκλῳ τοῦ πύργου; Βλέπω, φημί, κυρία. Ὁ πύργος οὗτος ὑπὸ τούτων βαστάζεται κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ Κυρίου. 3. ἄκουε νῦν τὰς ἐνεργείας αὐτῶν. ἡ μὲν πρώτη αὐτῶν, ἡ κρατοῦσα τὰς χεῖρας, Πίστις καλεῖται· διὰ ταύτης σώζονται οἱ ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ. 4. ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα, ἡ περιεζωσμένη καὶ ἀνδριζομένη, Ἐγκράτεια καλεῖται· αὕτη θυγάτηρ ἐστὶν τῆς Πίστεως. ὃς ἂν οὖν ἀκολουθήσῃ αὐτῇ, μακάριος γίνεται ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι πάντων τῶν πονηρῶν ἔργων ἀφέξεται, πιστεύων ὅτι, ἐὰν ἀφέξηται πάσης ἐπιθυμίας πονηρᾶς, κληρονομήσει ζωὴν αἰώνιον. 5. Αἱ δὲ ἕτεραι, κυρία, τίνες εἰσίν; Θυγατέρες ἀλλήλων εἰσίν. καλοῦνται δὲ ἡ μὲν Ἁπλότης, ἡ δὲ Ἐπιστήμη, ἡ δὲ Ἀκακία, ἡ δὲ Σεμνότης, ἡ δὲ Ἀγάπη. ὅταν οὖν τὰ ἔργα τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῶν πάντα ποιήσῃς, δύνασαι ζῆσαι. 6. Ἤθελον, φημί, γνῶναι, κυρία, τίς τίνα δύναμιν ἔχει αὐτῶν. Ἄκουε, φησίν, τὰς δυνάμεις ἃς ἔχουσιν. 7. κρατοῦνται δὲ ὑπ᾽ ἀλλήλων αἱ δυνάμεις αὐτῶν καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν ἀλλήλαις, καθὼς καὶ γεγεννημέναι εἰσίν. ἐκ τῆς Πίστεως γεννᾶται Ἐγκράτεια, ἐκ τῆς Ἐγκρατείας Ἁπλότης, ἐκ τῆς Ἁπλότητος Ἀκακία, ἐκ τῆς Ἀκακίας Σεμνότης, ἐκ τῆς Σεμνότητος Ἐπιστήμη, ἐκ τῆς Ἐπιστήμης Ἀγάπη. τούτων οὖν τὰ ἔργα ἁγνὰ καὶ σεμνὰ καὶ θεῖά ἐστιν. 8. ὃς ἂν οὖν δουλεύσῃ ταύταις καὶ ἰσχύσῃ κρατῆσαι τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν, ἐν τῷ πύργῳ ἕξει τὴν κατοίκησιν μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων τοῦ Θεοῦ. 9. ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὴν περὶ τῶν καιρῶν, εἰ ἤδη συντέλειά ἐστιν. ἡ δὲ ἀνέκραγε φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγουσα· Ἀσύνετε ἄνθρωπε, οὐχ ὁρᾷς τὸν πύργον ἔτι οἰκοδομούμενον; ὡς ἐὰν οὖν συντελεσθῇ ὁ πύργος οἰκοδομούμενος, ἔχει τέλος. ἀλλὰ ταχὺ ἐποικοδομηθήσεται. μηκέτι με ἐπερώτα μηδέν· ἀρκετή σοι ἡ ὑπόμνησις αὕτη καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις, καὶ ἡ ἀνακαίνωσις τῶν πνευμάτων ὑμῶν. 10. ἀλλ᾽ οὐ σοὶ μόνῳ ἀπεκαλύφθη, ἀλλ᾽ ἵνα πᾶσιν δηλώσῃς αὐτά. 11. μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας—νοῆσαί σε γὰρ δεῖ πρῶτον, ἐντέλλομαι δέ σοι πρῶτον, Ἑρμᾶ, τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἃ σοι μέλλω λέγειν— †λαλῆσαι† αὐτὰ [πάντα] εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῶν ἁγίων, ἵνα ἀκούσαντες αὐτὰ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθαρισθῶσιν ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ σὺ δὲ μετ᾽ αὐτῶν.

translation.text:
When[1], then, I had stopped questioning her about all these things, she says to me, “Do you want to see something else?” And because I was eager to behold it, I became very glad to see.

Looking at me, she smiled and says to me, “Do you see seven women around the tower?” “I do, lady,” I said. “This tower is supported by these women at the Lord’s command.

Now hear their functions.[1] The first of them, the one clasping her hands,[2] is called Faith; through her the chosen of God are saved. And the second[2], the one girded about and acting bravely,[3] is called Self-control; she is the daughter of Faith. Whoever, then, follows her becomes blessed in his life, because he will refrain from all evil works, believing that if he refrains from every evil desire he will inherit eternal life.”

“But the others, lady, who are they?” “They are daughters of one another. And they are called Simplicity, Knowledge, Innocence, Dignity, and Love. Whenever, then, you do all the works of their mother, you are able to live.”

“I wanted,” I said, “to know, lady, what power each of them has.” “Hear,” she says, “the powers they have. Their powers are held together by one another, and they follow one another, just as they were born: from Faith is born Self-control, from Self-control Simplicity, from Simplicity Innocence, from Innocence Dignity, from Dignity Knowledge, and from Knowledge Love. So, then, the works of these are pure and dignified and divine. Whoever, then, serves these and proves able to hold fast to their works will have his dwelling in the tower with the holy ones of God.”

And I kept asking her about the times—whether it is already the end. But she cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Senseless man, do you not see that the tower is still being built? Whenever, then, the tower is completed in its building, it comes to an end. But it will be built up quickly. Do not question me any further; this reminder and the renewal of your spirits are enough for you and for the holy ones.

But it was not revealed to you alone, but so that you may make them known to all. After three days—for first you must understand, and I first command you, Hermas, the words I am about to say to you—speak them all into the ears of the holy ones, so that, after hearing them and doing them, they may be cleansed from their evils[b][a][3], and you also with them.”

footnotes.text: Greek andrizomenē means 'acting bravely' or 'showing courage'; literally it carries a 'be manly/courageous' nuance.
Or 'this reminder is enough for you and for the holy ones, and for the renewal of your spirits.'.

lexical_decisions.rationale: In the tower image the sense is structural support. 'Supported' keeps the picture clear without weakening the metaphor.
The term describes what each personified virtue does. 'Functions' is clear and concrete in English.
As a personified virtue in Hermas, 'Faith' is the most natural rendering and matches the genealogical sequence that follows.
Self-restraint is the moral force of the virtue here, and 'Self-control' is the clearest modern English equivalent.
Hermas uses the term in an ethical sense close to singleness and straightforwardness; 'Simplicity' preserves the traditional moral register.
The virtue names build a chain of moral character; 'Innocence' is readable and keeps the ethical sense.
The term denotes honorable seriousness; 'Dignity' works naturally in the virtue list while preserving the elevated tone.
Standard rendering and the right one for the closing virtue in the sequence.
The point is having one’s settled place in the tower. 'Dwelling' keeps the symbolic and eschatological force.
The question is eschatological. 'The end' is plain English and fits the tower-completion image.
The noun marks inward renewal of life/spirit; 'renewal' is the best idiomatic rendering.
Hermas uses cleansing language for moral purification; 'cleansed' preserves that imagery.

theological_decisions.issue: Personified virtues as supporting agents of the tower
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Retain them as real personified virtues rather than reducing them to abstractions only.
alternative_readings: Flatten into abstract qualities without personification
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas presents the women both symbolically and dramatically. Preserving the personification keeps the visionary force of the passage.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render Faith as the means 'through' which God’s chosen are saved.
alternative_readings: Render more weakly as mere association with faith
theological_decisions.rationale: The preposition διά marks instrumentality/means; the line presents Faith as the God-appointed channel in the allegory.

theological_decisions.issue: The end and the tower’s completion
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Preserve the tower-completion image as the sign of the end.
alternative_readings: Over-interpret the tower immediately as a later ecclesial system
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas itself ties the end to the completion of the tower image; the translation should preserve the symbolism before later interpretation.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally excellent, but contains a mistranslation of 'κρατοῦσα τὰς χεῖρας' as 'strong hands' rather than 'clasping her hands'. A few minor adjustments were made to improve English phrasing ('whether it is already the end', 'it comes to an end').
issues_found: Mistranslation: 'ἡ κρατοῦσα τὰς χεῖρας' means 'the one holding/clasping her hands', not 'the one with the strong hands'.
Awkward English: 'whether the end is already' for 'εἰ ἤδη συντέλειά ἐστιν' is unnatural; 'whether it is already the end' is better.
Literalism: 'ἔχει τέλος' rendered as 'it has an end' is slightly clunky; 'it comes to an end' is more idiomatic.
Grammar: 'ἀπεκαλύφθη' is singular ('it was revealed'), but the draft rendered it as plural ('these things were revealed').

translation.text: “I wanted,” I said, “to know, lady, what power each of them has.” “Hear,” she says, “the powers they have. Their powers are held together by one another, and they follow one another, just as they were born: from Faith is born Self-control, from Self-control Simplicity, from Simplicity Innocence, from Innocence Dignity, from Dignity Knowledge, and from Knowledge Love. So, then, the works of these are pure and dignified and divine. Whoever, then, serves these and proves able to hold fast to their works will have his dwelling in the tower with the holy ones of God.”
